value: touch genes TCH3, TCH4, CML24 and CML39 induced 0.5 to 1 h after soft mechanical stimulation (10 successive rubbings)
units: transcript induction (qPCR; direction only in text)
method: leaves of A. thaliana Col-0 gently rubbed between thumb and forefinger without pressing; touch-gene transcripts by qPCR (reference gene At4g26410) in untreated and soft-mechanical-stimulation (SMS) leaves
conditions: Col-0 wild type; SMS repeated 10 successive times for Figure 2C; qPCR n = 3 (mean ± SD), repeated three times with similar results; no force measured; plant age for the qPCR not captured (inoculated leaves came from 4-week-old plants, cameleon imaging used 16 to 21-day-old plants). The text gives no fold changes (they are in Figure 2C) and reports no touch gene among these four as not induced. The same paper reports the induced resistance to Botrytis cinerea was transient (about half lost when inoculated 8 h after SMS, fully susceptible at 24 h) and that SMS was followed by a rapid change in intracellular calcium (cameleon and aequorin lines, transgenic reporters).

method: gentle manual touch (three to four mature rosette leaves per plant bent back and forth four times); transcripts by qPCR before touch and at 5, 15, 30 min and 1 h after
conditions: Col-0 plants, 18 days old for the short-term touch (grown in soil under continuous light, about 150 µmol m-2 s-1, 22 °C); no tool or force given; four biological replicates per analysis. The 17 genes (SRGs) were chosen from the authors' earlier sound-vibration work (500 Hz, 1 h), not from a touch screen. The Discussion states six of them were not up-regulated by touch at any time point; eight were highly up-regulated at 15 min. Five days of repeated touch (twice daily, 15-day-old plants, harvest at 20 days) up-regulated MSL3, MSL7, MSL9 and MCA2 in two independent experiments.
